interest: This document is of significant interest to historians of interwar intelligence, Scandinavian security, and aerial folklore, as it documents U.S. diplomatic tracking of the widespread 1933–1934 'ghost flier' or 'mystery plane' wave across Northern Europe. It illustrates that State Department officials and diplomats in Helsinki took reports of unidentified aircraft seriously enough to log them under Japanese military intelligence and cross-reference them to Soviet military and narcotics tracking files, reflecting contemporaneous anxieties over covert espionage, border reconnaissance, and smuggling operations during a period of escalating global tensions.
overview: This file (894.20260D, File 479) comprises a single Department of State 'List of Papers' docket sheet (Form DS-46) dated October 12, 1945, cataloguing records under the subject 'Japanese Military Activities in Finland.' The sheet registers sub-number 2, referencing Despatch No. 109 sent on February 14, 1934, by U.S. Minister Edward Albright from Finland, routed to the Divisions of Far Eastern Affairs and Eastern European Affairs. The entry details reports of 'mystery planes' operating over Finland and Scandinavia, conjectured to be of Japanese or Russian origin, with notation cross-referencing State Department decimal files concerning Soviet military matters (861.20260d, 861.20257d) and narcotics trafficking (861.114-Narcotics).

subfiles.summary: A Department of State 'List of Papers' sheet (Form DS-46) for decimal file 894.20260D, dated October 12, 1945, concerning Japanese military activities in Finland. It records entry sub-number 2, which catalogs Despatch No. 109 sent by Edward Albright from Finland on February 14, 1934, and routed to the Far Eastern and Eastern European divisions. The recorded despatch reported on alleged mystery planes observed flying over Finland and Scandinavia, suspected of being of Russian or Japanese origin, and notes cross-references to Soviet military and narcotics files.
